semantic_adjudication.reason: NL4 ('the system can transition to DoorShutWithItem if the door is closed with zero time set or to ReadytoCook if cooking time is entered') frames the two exits as alternatives that must remain distinguishable. The exact closed source and inspection facts confirm both transitions (line:23 -> tr_0007 on event Door_Closed_with_0_time, line:24 -> tr_0008 on event Time_Set) have guard=null, so no explicit guard expression exists to check for disjointness via a data-guard predicate. However, since each transition is triggered by a distinct, exactly bound named event rather than sharing a single event discriminated by competing guards, the two alternatives are already operationally exclusive by event selection: an incoming Door_Closed_with_0_time event cannot also be a Time_Set event. This is an exact structural fact (distinct event refs on each transition) rather than a conceivable hidden mechanism, so it is a genuine rebuttal candidate to the guard-disjointness reading, though it does not itself supply a formal guard predicate. The strongest alternative reading is that event-based discrimination fully satisfies NL4's disjointness intent even absent a populated guard field; this survives as a competent rebuttal supported by the exact distinct-event-ref facts, while the predicate-null status remains a W-boundary matter rather than deciding the semantic question here.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The two DoorOpenWithItem alternatives are discriminated by two distinct, exactly bound named events (Door_Closed_with_0_time vs Time_Set) rather than by competing guards on a shared event, so they are already mutually exclusive by event identity alone, which may fully satisfy NL4's disjointness intent even though no guard field is populated on either transition.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL4 requires the two DoorOpenWithItem exits (to DoorShutWithItem on zero time set, and to ReadytoCook on cooking time entered) to be distinguishable/mutually exclusive alternatives; the exact source shows both transitions (tr_0007/tr_0008, lines 23/24) carry guard=null and are discriminated only by distinct event identities (Door_Closed_with_0_time vs Time_Set), so no formal guard predicate encodes the 'zero time set' vs 'cooking time entered' distinction.
